      - heading "Understand Area of Triangle Using Coordinates" [level=2]
  - text: CLASS 10 · COORDINATE GEOMETRY
  - heading "Area of Triangle Using Coordinates" [level=1]
  - paragraph: Compute the area of a triangle from its vertex coordinates using the determinant method.
  - paragraph: Interpret the result's sign to determine orientation and use absolute value for geometric area.
  - navigation:
    - button "INTERACT"
    - button "LEARN"
    - button "EXAMPLE"
    - button "FORMULA"
    - button "PRACTICE"
  - main:
    - heading "Build and explore your triangle" [level=2]
    - complementary:
      - heading "● A (x1, y1)" [level=3]
      - text: x1
      - spinbutton "Vertex A x": "1"
      - text: y1
      - spinbutton "Vertex A y": "1"
      - heading "● B (x2, y2)" [level=3]
      - text: x2
      - spinbutton "Vertex B x": "5"
      - text: y2
      - spinbutton "Vertex B y": "1"
      - heading "● C (x3, y3)" [level=3]
      - text: x3
      - spinbutton "Vertex C x": "3"
      - text: y3
      - spinbutton "Vertex C y": "4"
      - button "Reset triangle":
        - img
        - text: Reset triangle
    - article:
      - img "Draggable coordinate-area triangle": D (3, 1) A (1, 1) B (5, 1) C (3, 4)
      - checkbox "Show base–height" [checked]
      - text: Show base–height
      - checkbox "Show coordinates" [checked]
      - text: Show coordinates
    - complementary:
      - heading "Determinant method" [level=2]
      - heading "① Determinant (2 × signed area)" [level=3]
      - strong: "| x₁ y₁ 1 | | x₂ y₂ 1 | = 12 | x₃ y₃ 1 |"
      - paragraph: 1(1−4) + 5(4−1) + 3(1−1)
      - paragraph: = 12
      - heading "② Signed area = ½ × 12 = 6 sq. units" [level=3]
      - heading "Orientation & area" [level=3]
      - radio "Signed area mode" [checked]
      - text: Signed area (orientation matters)
      - strong: 6 sq. units (counterclockwise)
      - radio "Absolute area mode"
      - text: Absolute area (geometric area)
      - strong: 6 sq. units
    - text: Base AB = 4 units Height from C to AB = 3 units Area = ½ × 4 × 3 = 6 sq. units
    - complementary:
      - text: 💡
      - strong: Drag any vertex
      - text: (or edit the coordinates) to see how the area and orientation change in real time.
    - article:
      - heading "◎ Why it works" [level=2]
      - paragraph: The determinant is twice the signed area of the triangle.
      - strong: "| x₁ y₁ 1 | | x₂ y₂ 1 | = 2 × (signed area) | x₃ y₃ 1 |"
      - paragraph: Positive → counterclockwise (CCW)
      - paragraph: Negative → clockwise (CW)
      - paragraph: Taking absolute value gives geometric area.
    - article:
      - heading "♙ Worked example" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Find the area of △ABC with A(1,1), B(5,1), C(3,4).
      - paragraph: Determinant = 12
      - paragraph: Signed area = ½ × 12 = 6 sq. units (counterclockwise)
      - paragraph: Area = ½ |12| = 6 sq. units
      - emphasis:
        - img
        - text: "Matches base–height: ½ × 4 × 3 = 6."
    - article:
      - heading "⚠ Common mistake" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Forgetting the absolute value.
      - paragraph: Signed area may be negative, but geometric area cannot be negative.
      - text: "Correct: Area = ½ |Determinant| Not correct: Area = ½ (Determinant)"
    - article:
      - 'heading "♜ Challenge: swap two vertices" [level=2]'
      - paragraph: Swap B and C. What happens?
      - paragraph: "New order: A(1,1), C(3,4), B(5,1)"
      - button "Apply swap"
      - strong: "Result: Signed area becomes -6 sq. units, but absolute area remains 6."
      - text: Why does the orientation change but the area stay the same?
      - textbox "Orientation explanation":
        - /placeholder: Type your explanation here...
